raw_response:
I farm 7 mu in Quzhou, been at it for 26 years since I was 20. My father taught me, and I learned the rest by watching what works on the neighbors' fields. I never went to school, but I know this soil.

This year I keep my 5 mu for wheat-maize and 2 mu for cotton, same as always. Changing too much is asking for trouble.

For wheat, I sow in October. I buy improved seed, 15 jin per mu, costs me 50 yuan. Before sowing I plough deep and spread one full 50-jin bag of compound fertilizer on each mu — that costs 140 yuan per mu. When spring comes and the wheat turns green, I broadcast half a bag of urea, 25 jin per mu, another 60 yuan. That gives me about 22 kg of nitrogen per mu, and 8 kg each of phosphorus and potassium from the compound bag. Last year Chen used less fertilizer and his wheat was thin and yellow. Not me. Better to spend the money than lose the harvest. I irrigate three times from my well: once before the winter freeze, once at jointing, and once when the grain is filling. Two sprays for weeds and bugs. If the weather holds, I expect 480 kg per mu.

Wheat comes off in June, and I plant maize the same week — no time to waste. I rotary till quick because the season is short. Hybrid maize seed, 4 jin per mu, 35 yuan. I put 25 jin of compound fertilizer per mu at sowing, then side-dress 25 jin of urea when the plants are knee-high. That is about 16 kg nitrogen, 4 kg phosphorus, and 4 kg potassium per mu. Two irrigations: one right after sowing if it doesn't rain, and one when the tassels come out. Two pesticide sprays. I expect 520 kg per mu.

My 2 mu of cotton gets ploughed deep in April because cotton roots need loose soil. Hybrid seed, one bag per mu. Base fertilizer is one full 50-jin bag of compound per mu. I top-dress twice with urea, 20 jin each time. That comes to about 18 kg nitrogen, 8 kg phosphorus, and 8 kg potassium per mu. Three irrigations through the summer. Five sprays because bollworm and aphids always come. I expect around 260 kg per mu of seed cotton.

My wife and oldest son work at the factory in town, so during busy times it's me and my daughter. I hire old Zhang for about 10 days at harvest, pay him by the day. Fertilizer prices went up again, but I saw what happened to Li from the next village when he cut back last year — his maize ears were half empty and his cotton bolls dropped early. I will not make that mistake. A bad harvest means I can't pay for my daughter's school supplies. Wasting some fertilizer is just a cost.
